searchText: Ended up super busy today, so probably won't get 2718 updated until tomorrow. Tentative plane: * Split the EIP in two, one for the new transaction/receipt formats and one for the new legacy wrapper transaction type. * Remove everything about deprecation of the legacy format from the EIP. * Extract the devp2p changes into their own EIP with improved definitions that better align with reality. * Change transaction/receipt root merkle path back to an RLP encoded integer * Create EIP for JSON-RPC endpoints for new transaction format (naming welcome) * Update EIP-2930 to be in line with latest iteration of 2718 * Update EIP-2711 to be in line with latest iteration of 2718 (and potentially revamp it with help from <@!425279588009246720>) Was going to implement "EIP-2565 option 2", thought it was just changing a constant. Nope: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/2955 Do we know if the author (Kelly Olson, I think?) is on discord? yes i will DM you his discord cc: <@!598593394985533473> He (they all) should have been pinged by the merge-bot, if nothing else There were also some relevant comments on https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/2892 Breakout-room discussion meeting#2 Date & Time: Monday 14 September 2020, at 14:00 UTC Agenda: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/207 Would it make sense having specific rooms instead for "transaction types", "repricing", etc. and have them discussed that way? Now we have discussed transaction types in 3 places (allcoredevs, eips, breakout-room). Otherwise I'm not sure what this room serves beyond what can be accomplished with <#745077610685661265>. Just a question, not sure what is the best solution ^^ I personally don't mind just using <#745077610685661265>: if people don't care it's pretty easy to skim past a large conversation on a specific topic. Just slightly annoying that there is no threading, but it's not like we often have multiple simultaneous in-depth conversations on the channel For me, there are already a bit too many channels to even try to keep up. Maybe we can let the "breakout-room" become the "acd nitty gritty", so that ACD is kept fairly low-volume, and deeper discussions and long technical discussions on "stuff related to ACD" go into "the channel currently known as breakout-room" I started mute channels quite aggressively from the beginning, and now I even had to temporarily mute <#745077610685661265> and <#688075293562503241> for few hours, and I don't feel bad 🙂 were we wanting EIP-2718 to introduce a replacement for the legacy tx format? e.g. the exact same except its tx type is prepended to RLP encoded tx before hashing i believe this would allow future wallets to disregard the legacy hashing format completely If possible I believe we should aim for eventually depreciation of the current/legacy format. Likely on a longish timeline after eip-2718 is live to give time for the many many many things that will need to be updated. I've been considering something like a time bomb that slowly ratchets up the intrinsic transaction cost over the course of 18 months to ensure nobody is still using it at the point of full depreciation maybe it makes sense then for this new "standard" tx type to be the 1559 type? that way, the legacy tx will fall off whenever 1559 txs take over i think you can never fully deprecate it, given hardware wallets or perhaps there could be some sort of system contract which could receive and process old style transactions, while keeping the protocol clean i was just thinking the same (regarding hardware wallets), but then how does 1559 deal with this fact? i'm not sure how 1559 deals with it to be honest i assumed it would mostly a parallel system and at some point the old-style-pool would be extremely limited in capacity my understanding was that the % of the block gas limit for 1559 transactions increases over a fixed period of time until only 1559 txs are valid (looks like the eip currently says this migration period is 800k blocks) i think you definitely could wrap the old-style-tx into a 1559-tx where the gas payer account is the one specified in 1559-tx, and you may or may not adhere the gas limit from old-style-tx i know there was a lot of discussion around sender-vs-gas-payer transactions and the different combinations of limit+price (of the sender vs. gas payer) > i think you definitely could wrap the old-style-tx into a 1559-tx where the gas payer account is the one specified in 1559-tx, and you may or may not adhere the gas limit from old-style-tx This seems like a great idea, would make the change less draconian so I actually enabled that possiblity in the hackmd I shared, only because the document doesn't state restrictions yet 🙂

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content:
Ended up super busy today, so probably won't get 2718 updated until tomorrow.  Tentative plane:
* Split the EIP in two, one for the new transaction/receipt formats and one for the new legacy wrapper transaction type.
* Remove everything about deprecation of the legacy format from the EIP.
* Extract the devp2p changes into their own EIP with improved definitions that better align with reality.
* Change transaction/receipt root merkle path back to an RLP encoded integer
* Create EIP for JSON-RPC endpoints for new transaction format (naming welcome)
* Update EIP-2930 to be in line with latest iteration of 2718
* Update EIP-2711 to be in line with latest iteration of 2718 (and potentially revamp it with help from <@!425279588009246720>)
